Independent BFS checks all n<=18 facet cases and mod-two boundary ranks in nine cases. Results limited to finite n<=35.

originality.rationale: The exact proposed borderline wedge appears as a conjecture in Bayer et al. (arXiv:2304.13675), whose original numerical range was k<=15. The separate k=16 integral homotopy result and all-k face-vector/Euler results are acknowledged as prior. Exhaustive new acyclic Morse and signed integral boundary certificates extend rigorously through k=30, with 14 new parameters k=17..30, not implied by Euler characteristic or adjacent diagonals. Actual semantic-index and primary-literature queries inspected. A possible unindexed equivalent calculation remains a residual bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent result could be in an unindexed work or inaccessible source.
For two of the indexed related findings, only public statements/summaries rather than complete full text were inspected.

The finite executable certificate relies on a correct implementation of graph facets, Hasse orientation and integer gradient signs; these have been explicitly rechecked and representative independent tests performed.

value.rationale: Addresses a precisely stated, nontrivial published homotopy conjecture for the first borderline squared-cycle k-cut complexes, in the still-unresolved finite range k=17..30 beyond published numerical checks k<=15 and independently established k=16. The exact integral degree certificate is stronger than an all-k Euler formula; it confirms no torsion and explicit sphere counts for 28 natural consecutive cases. It is not a general theorem or routine recomputation of a known table; its finite nature is disclosed.
